title: IsItLegit: how it works
sub: A technical deep dive: intake, the pipeline, the checks, Meta's models, the verdict, the trust network, storage and the app.

scenes.title: What it does
scenes.sub: Forward a suspicious email. Get a verdict with the evidence.

scenes.title: The problem, and the answer
items: Phishing and business email compromise get past Microsoft 365 and other filters every day.
The costliest case: an invoice from a real supplier whose bank details were quietly changed.
IsItLegit takes a forwarded email, an upload or a voice note, and runs an investigation.
The answer is a plain-language verdict ({fact.verdictClasses}), the top three reasons, and what to do now.
Every claim cites a piece of evidence; hard rules set a floor the model cannot lower.
Each chapter here is marked shipped, partly built or planned, measured from src/ and the stamped plan.

scenes.title: From a forward to a case
items: Forward to {fact.intakeAddress}; Cloudflare Email Routing hands it to the Worker's email() handler.
Only members are processed: the sender must belong to a verified domain or address; anything else is {fact.dropNoReply}, so no backscatter.
Messages over {fact.emailMaxBytes} are refused before they are read; machine mail is never answered, so two responders cannot loop.
Each delivery is claimed in D1 first by Message-ID or SHA-256; the same mail within {fact.dupWindow} is a duplicate.
The Workflow's {fact.instanceId}, so a retry or a replay never makes two cases.
Each organisation gets {fact.dailyCaps} cases a day by default.
{fact.forwardAttach} It keeps the original headers that authentication checks need.

scenes.sub: Status: shipped, with the verdict step still a stub until the agent lands.

scenes.title: Durable by design
items: Each step retries: {fact.retryLimit} backoff, with a {fact.stepTimeout} attempt timeout.
Step results are cached by the Workflow, so a paid model call is never repeated after a later failure.
A budget refusal is never retried.
A step that fails after its last attempt {fact.partialCase} and names the step, and the reply still goes out.
A cron at {fact.cronReconcile} settles uncertain mail sends and sweeps stuck intake claims.

scenes.sub: Status: partly built. Authentication and header checks are shipped; domain and content checks are planned.

scenes.title: One evidence model for everything
scenes.sub: Every check is a pure function that returns evidence the verdict must cite.
lines: ids:       E1, E2, E3 ... cited by the verdict
failure:   a check that fails becomes not_checked, never a silence or a guess

scenes.title: The checks
rows: Trusted Authentication-Results, SPF, DKIM, DMARC with alignment ({fact.authAlign})
ARC chain, display name versus address, Reply-To, Return-Path, first-time sender
Lookalike domains: the {fact.lookalikeSkeleton} plus edit distance against a brand table
Domain age and newly registered flag ({fact.rdap})
Hidden text, including {fact.hiddenText}, treated as evidence against the mail

scenes.title: Outside opinions, weighed
items: {fact.webRisk} (uris.search only), free up to {fact.webRiskFree}.
{fact.cf112}, a malware-blocking resolver over DNS-over-HTTPS, as a second opinion.
Weight follows granularity: an exact URL hit is strong, a domain medium, an IP weak.
{fact.listNotAlone} It must agree with our own evidence.
Counter-signals pull the other way: a verified domain, a top-sites listing, DMARC alignment. The report shows both sides.

scenes.title: The floor
scenes.text: Critical evidence {fact.floorRule}. The model may raise severity, never lower it, so an injected 'this is safe' still loses.

scenes.title: One client, strict rules
items: Every call goes through AI Gateway {fact.gatewayName}, authenticated, logging metadata only, logs kept {fact.gatewayRetention}.
{fact.storeFalse} is forced on every Responses call, and {fact.standardOnly}, never contributor ones.
A model sent to the wrong endpoint is refused before the network.
A budget guard reserves the cost before each call and refuses past a cap; every result is validated with zod.
Results are cached by artefact hash in KV, so the same screenshot or PDF costs nothing the second time.
The first live Spark call measured {fact.liveSpark} tokens in and out, with the cost read back.

scenes.title: Prompt injection is defended by structure
items: Email text, PDF text and page text reach a model only inside {fact.untrustedBlocks}.
{fact.noModelRecipients} Tools are read-only.
The hard floor means injected instructions cannot lower a verdict.
Injection fixtures sit in the test set, so a regression is caught.

scenes.title: The costliest fraud, checked field by field
items: Extract {fact.invoiceFields} as structured JSON.
A per-organisation supplier ledger holds known suppliers and their verified bank details.
Changed bank details, a changed domain or 'we have changed banks' wording is {fact.bankChange} evidence, with a fixed instruction: phone the number in your own records.
Payment documents (invoices, proofs of payment, bank letters) are checked for producer, incremental edits, fonts and dates.
A proof-of-payment check can show a document is likely doctored, never that a payment cleared.

scenes.title: The trust network
scenes.sub: Status: planned. Protection for businesses whose name is used against their customers.

scenes.title: Registered identity
items: A business registers and verifies its {fact.trustProtected}.
Anyone can forward mail claiming to be that business; the verdict compares it with the registered identity.
The {fact.bankPrivacy}: a checker sees only match or no match, {fact.cpLimit}.
Closed-loop verification: the agent {fact.closedLoop} to confirm a bank change.
The email signature badge links to {fact.badgeUrl}; the real proof is the forwarded message's DKIM, SPF and DMARC.
The website seal is a frame whose {fact.sealFrame} names only verified domains.

items: {fact.betterAuth} on D1: email magic link, passkeys and organisations with roles {fact.roles}.
The organisation comes {fact.orgScope}, and membership is checked on every request.
Invite codes are redeemed in one atomic SQL update ({fact.inviteAtomic}); a {fact.trialDays}-day trial.

Sign-in is limited to {fact.signinRate} requests per IP per 10 minutes, with scanner-safe links so Microsoft 365 link scanners cannot burn a token.
Report links are HMAC-signed and expire after {fact.reportLinkDays} days.
The admin console sits behind {fact.accessAdmin}; the marketing site is {fact.astro} (planned).
